title: Woad
transcription:
Woad

What's the use of wearing braces
hats and pants and boots and laces?
These are things you buy in places
down on Brampton road.
What's the use of shirts of cotton,
studs that always get forgotten?
Things like these are simply rotten.
Better far is Woad.

Woad's the stuff you showman.
Woad to scare your foe man.
Boil it to a brilliant blue
and rub it on your back and your abdomen.
Ancient Britain never hit on
anything as good as woad to fit on
Neck or knee or where you sit on,
tailors you be blowed.

Romans came across the channel
all dressed up in tin and flannel
Half a pint of woad per mannel
dress you more than these.
Saxons you can waste your stitches
building beds for bugs in britches
We have woad to clothe us witches
not a nest for fleas.

Romans keep you armors,
Saxons your pajamees
Hairy coats were made for goats, gorillas, yaks, retriever dogs, and llamas.
March up snowdens with your woad on
never mind if you get rained or snowed on,
Never want a button sewed on.
Go it ancient Bs.
notes: Draft song-level split from visual page transcription. Source page note: Draft visual transcription from photographed page spread. Some small words are uncertain because of image softness, especially in McPhearson's Farewell and Woad.
